commits.pr_title: [XPU] limit FA kernel block size to multipleOf 64
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
On XPU platform, `flash_attn_varlen_func` prefers `block_size` multipleOf 64 from performance perspective and we originally respect it by adding path in [`get_preferred_block_size`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py#L323). But as introduction of [`prepare_kernel_block_size`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/worker/utils.py#L458), the final kernel block size changes to small numbers such as 16, 32 which are not actually preferred ones on XPU platform. This PR enforces the preference and adds warning if final kernel block size is not as expected.

Take `Microsoft/Phi-3.5-mini-instruct` for example, #53007 caused final kernel_block_size changed to `16` from previous `64`, as it picks primary block size for SWA layers which changes KV cache Spec info. XPU will follow the `prepare_kernel_block_size` flow but inject specific logic like [update_block_size_for_backend](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/platforms/xpu.py#L425), [get_preferred_block_size](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py#L373), and here `get_preferred_kernel_block_size`.

## Test Plan
```
python3 examples/basic/offline_inference/generate.py --model Microsoft/Phi-3.5-mini-instruct  --enforce-eager --max-model-len 4096 --trust_remote_code 
```

## Test Result
previous without `multipleOf[64]` limitation, it will use kernel block-size `16`:
```
(EngineCore pid=14829) WARNING 09-17 03:28:59 [attn_utils.py:259] On XPU platform, current selected kernel block size is not fully optimized: kernel_block_size=16, backend=<class 'vllm.v1.attention.backends.flash_attn.FlashAttentionBackend'>, kv_cache_spec=SlidingWindowSpec(block_size=16, num_kv_heads=32, head_size=96, dtype=torch.bfloat16, head_size_v=96, kv_quant_mode=<KVQuantMode.NONE: 0>, page_size_padded=None, num_head_slots=None, state_content_bytes=None, tokens_per_state=1, sliding_window=262144, extra_retained_tokens=0)
```
after:
No warning happens indicating that block size `64` is used.
**Note that if user explicitly sets block size using `--block-size 16`, it will be respected and warning will be printed.**

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][RecoverSSM] Correct aligned state indices at exact block boundaries
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

**Upstream full-model evaluation pending.**

Fix RecoverSSM align-mode final-state indexing at exact Mamba block boundaries in both the KDA commit planner and V2 postprocessing. Fixes #59933.

## Claims

- At an exact boundary, commit and record the state for the block containing the last accepted token, rather than advancing to the next block.
- Retain the zero-length clamp and block-table upper bound; leave non-align behavior unchanged.
- Extend existing numeric-reference and mixed-batch CUDA tests to cover boundary neighbors, request remapping, and first/second exact boundaries.

## Validation

Base: `bd42276e1e25f540f019381c65994120158aa2a1`. NVIDIA RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (SM89), PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA runtime 13.0. Tests use candidate source with the installed GPU wheel's compiled extensions and missing vendor interfaces linked into ignored paths.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py -k recoverssm -q --tb=short
```

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New tests, original production code | 4 failed, 15 passed; 11.98s |
| New tests, fixed production code | 19 passed; 6.51s |
| Human personal test run | 19 passed, 101 deselected, 14 warnings; 7.62s; user screenshot |
| Changed-file pre-commit | All applicable hooks passed, including mypy and test tethering |
| `git diff --check` | Passed |

Both pytest runs deselected 101 unrelated tests and reported 14 existing Torch deprecation warnings. Two baseline failures were KDA committed-state comparisons against `naive_recurrent_kda`; two were incorrect V2 state columns at totals 8 and 16. The KDA test compares all state slots, including slots that should remain unchanged, as well as convolution state.

An additional metadata run was interrupted while waiting in a network socket (20 tests had passed); this is not a completed passing run. No upstream Kimi-K3 full-model accuracy/generation evaluation has been performed. The repository's Kimi-K3 GSM8K configuration requires TP4 hardware beyond this single laptop GPU. No throughput or latency claim is made.

## Details

Aligned state columns correspond to the block containing the last committed token. `total // block_size` advances prematurely when `total` is an exact multiple. Use `max(total - 1, 0) // block_size`, capped to the existing width limit, in both writer planning and recorded next-step state selection.

Credit: @seanphan reported #59933 with the downstream diagnosis/proposed arithmetic fix credited to @YulHeon. This patch independently reproduces the issue in upstream GPU tests and adds regression coverage. The reporter's downstream GLM A/B results are not claimed as our validation or as upstream Kimi-K3 evaluation.

Duplicate checks: issue body/comments, all-state PR search `59933 in:body` (no results), related RecoverSSM searches, and inspection of #56082. #56082 changes recovery performance/warmup and does not change these final-column expressions.

AI-assisted with Codex. **Human submitter confirmed line review and personally ran the relevant tests (19 passed, 7.62s). Opened for review at the human submitter's explicit request. Human line review and personal GPU/reference tests are complete; upstream full-model validation remains outstanding. Please help coordinate that evaluation before merging.**

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Read Ling quantization_config from top-level config for Bailing V3 VL
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL-fp4` fails at weight loading on every platform:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (3) must match the size of tensor b (12) at non-singleton dimension 1
  (routed_experts.py, _load_w2)
```

The routed experts are MXFP4 (`routed_experts_quant_method: mxfp4`). `_configure_ling_fp8_quant_config` reads that from `config.quantization_config`, but the VL model builds its language model from `text_config`, which has no `quantization_config` (it lives on the top-level VL config). The helper returns early, `store_dtype` stays unset, and the experts get `Fp8MoEMethod` instead of `Mxfp4MoEMethod`. The same bug makes the model OOM at TP=1, because FP8 expert buffers are ~2x the MXFP4 size.

This PR makes the helper fall back to the current vLLM config's top-level `hf_config` when the config it receives has no `quantization_config`. Text-only Ling and the MTP draft (whose config already carries `quantization_config`) are unchanged.


## Test Plan

- Existing config tests: `pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_bailing_moe_v3_vl_config.py`
- End to end on Intel XPU (4x Arc Pro B70, TP=4, `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:nightly-29468dde`):
  - Serve: `vllm serve inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL-fp4 --dtype bfloat16 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 5756 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --trust-remote-code --enforce-eager --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' --no-enable-prefix-caching`, then one text and one image chat request.
  - Accuracy: `lm_eval --model vllm --model_args pretrained=inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL-fp4,tensor_parallel_size=4,dtype=bfloat16,trust_remote_code=True,max_model_len=4096,gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,enforce_eager=True --tasks gsm8k --batch_size auto`

## Test Result

Existing `tests/transformers_utils/test_bailing_moe_v3_vl_config.py`: ✓ 6/6 PASS

End to end (XPU, TP=4):

| | stock | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| MoE backend | `TRITON Fp8 MoE` | ✓ `XPU Mxfp4 MoE` |
| Load | FAIL, error above on all ranks | ✓ 16.51 GiB/rank, KV cache 693,767 tokens |
| Text / image chat | — | ✓ correct answers (`3+5-2` → `6`; red square top left, blue circle bottom right) |
| gsm8k (5-shot) flexible / strict | — | ✓ 0.8362 ± 0.0102 / 0.8249 ± 0.0105 |

For reference, the text sibling `Ling-3.0-flash-fp8` scores 0.8302 / 0.7688 on gsm8k.

commits.pr_title: [Fix] MiniMax: fix CUDA IPC handle exchange on cuda-bindings >= 13.4
commits.pr_body:
Fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58599, https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/issues/8931

### What's wrong

The MiniMax fused allreduce+RMSNorm kernel needs each GPU to read the other GPUs' memory directly. To set that up, every GPU allocates a buffer, gets a small 64-byte "IPC handle" for it, and sends that handle to the other GPUs. They then use it to open the buffer.

vLLM converted the handle to bytes and back through its .reserved field. In cuda-bindings 13.4 (part of cuda-python), NVIDIA removed that field from cudaIpcMemHandle_t, so the code now fails with:
AttributeError: 'cuda.bindings.runtime.cudaIpcMemHandle_t' object has no attribute 'reserved'


When that happens, vLLM falls back to the slower non-fused path, and test_minimax_reduce_rms_qk fails. It shows up in the torch-nightly CI lane because that environment installs cuda-bindings 13.4.x.

### The fix

Copy the 64 handle bytes through handle.getPtr(), the handle's memory address, using ctypes. Every cuda-bindings version supports it, so no version check is needed.

_ipc_handle_to_bytes(handle) reads the 64 bytes out of a handle.
_ipc_handle_from_bytes(raw) creates a new handle and copies the 64 bytes into it.
The fix is limited to vllm/model_executor/layers/minimax_rms_norm/lamport_workspace.py.


### Test plan
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_minimax_reduce_rms.py::test_minimax_reduce_rms_qk -k "2-"
Before: fails with the AttributeError above and logs "Falling back to the eager allreduce".
After: 6 passed, 12 skipped (the 4- and 8-GPU cases, since there are only 2 GPUs). The fallback message is gone, so the fused path runs.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Fix FlashInfer attention and ReplaySSM warmups on MRV2
commits.pr_body:
FlashInfer attention warmup:
- The warmup ran a hard-coded 16-token mixed dummy batch without clamping to `max_num_batched_tokens`. On V1 this tripped the `num_tokens <= max_num_tokens` assert; on MRV2 `make_dummy` silently sliced input buffers shorter than `query_start_loc`, failing later in FlashInfer forward (`prefill_query.shape[0] == num_prefill_tokens`). Seen on Blackwell, where FlashInfer is the default, e.g. `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_e2e.py`.
- MRV2's `_dummy_run` ignored `create_mixed_batch`, so the warmup never ran a mixed prefill+decode batch.

Add `mixed_batch_attention_warmup()`, used by the FlashInfer and MiniMax M3 MSA warmups. It clamps the token count, keeps the V1 mixed dummy batch, and on MRV2 uses `run_mixed_prefill_decode_warmup()` (skipping when that can't run). MRV2's `_dummy_run` now asserts the token budget like V1.

ReplaySSM autotune:
- MRV2 profile dummy runs drop Mamba metadata, so the FlashInfer ReplaySSM autotune never ran the ReplaySSM kernel on MRV2 and `valid_dummy_state_slots` had no effect. Keep Mamba metadata for profile runs that set `valid_dummy_state_slots`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Honor `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` for the KDA recurrent state
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`Glm5NextLinearAttention.get_state_dtype()` and `Glm5NextForCausalLM.get_mamba_state_dtype_from_config()` call `MambaStateDtypeCalculator.kda_state_dtype()` without the SSM cache dtype. As a result, the KDA recurrent state is always float32, and `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16` is **silently ignored** for GLM-5.3-Flash. Kimi-K3's KDA already passes it through.

This PR passes `cache_config.mamba_ssm_cache_dtype` in both places. `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` delegates to the causal-LM class, so it is fixed too.

Why it matters: with bfloat16 the recurrent state page halves. Mamba align-mode prefix caching sizes the attention block from that page, so at TP2 the block shrinks from 2304 to 1280 tokens. With speculative decoding, each running request holds `2 + num_speculative_tokens` state blocks per group, so on decode instances this state is what bounds concurrency.

## Test Plan

- New test `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_state_dtype.py`:
  - `auto` / `float32` / `bfloat16` must reach both the model-level and the layer-level recurrent-state dtype;
  - the bf16 case fails on main.
- Existing tests: `tests/models/glm5next`.
- End to end: GLM-5.3-Flash, TP2, B300, with `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16`:
  - the KV-cache spec now reports the bf16 state page;
  - teacher-forced NLL on long-context prompts is unchanged within run-to-run noise vs the float32 state.

## Test Result

- `tests/models/glm5next`: 14 passed.
- With bf16 state, a spec-decoding decode instance (K=4, P/D serving) fits ~1.25× more concurrent requests before running out of state blocks (≈64 → 80+).

AI assistance (Claude) was used; every line was reviewed and the tests above were run by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [MRV2] Switch CI tests still running on MRV1 unnecessarily
[Bugfix] Respect the configured offline chat template
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Use the template configured through `LLM(chat_template=...)` in `chat()` and `enqueue_chat()`. Explicit per-call templates continue to override the constructor default.

## Claims

- Both offline chat entry points use the configured template instead of silently falling back to the tokenizer template.
- Per-call template overrides retain their existing behavior.

## Validation

Real Qwen3-0.6B inference: both constructor-default cases fail on main, pass with this change, and fail again after reverting it. Both explicit override controls pass throughout. Applicable manual pre-commit hooks pass.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and original results</summary>

Baseline: `187a0eb98aa42341d703f83421d693fa7585581b`; candidate: `8535b1c179`. Hardware: one RTX 5090. Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Transformers 5.16.1; eager execution. This checks prompt construction and short generation, not benchmark accuracy.

Model revision: `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`.

```bash
hf download Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --revision c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca --local-dir model
```

With each code revision installed, save this as `repro.py` and run `.venv/bin/python repro.py result.json`:

```python
import json,sys,pathlib
from vllm import LLM,SamplingParams
MODEL='./model'
TEMPLATE="User: {{ messages[0]['content'] }}\nAssistant:"
OVERRIDE="Question: {{ messages[0]['content'] }}\nAnswer:"
def main():
 llm=LLM(model=MODEL,chat_template=TEMPLATE,enforce_eager=True,max_model_len=512,gpu_memory_utilization=0.25)
 tokenizer=llm.get_tokenizer();messages=[{'role':'user','content':'What is the capital of France?'}]
 results=[]
 for entry in ['chat','enqueue_chat']:
  for override in [None,OVERRIDE]:
   kwargs=dict(sampling_params=SamplingParams(temperature=0,max_tokens=4),use_tqdm=False)
   if override is not None:kwargs['chat_template']=override
   outputs=getattr(llm,entry)(messages,**kwargs)
   if entry=='enqueue_chat':outputs=llm.wait_for_completion(use_tqdm=False)
   expected=tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages,chat_template=override or TEMPLATE,tokenize=True,add_generation_prompt=True,return_dict=False)
   result=dict(entry=entry,override=override is not None,expected=expected,actual=outputs[0].prompt_token_ids,text=outputs[0].outputs[0].text)
   result['matches']=result['actual']==expected;results.append(result);print(json.dumps(result),flush=True)
 pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).write_text(json.dumps(results,indent=2))
 print('CHAT_TEMPLATE_PASSED' if all(r['matches'] for r in results) else 'CHAT_TEMPLATE_MISMATCH',flush=True)
if __name__=='__main__':main()
```
